about.title: Montebello Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Slip and fall injuries in Montebello often happen in places people pass through every day — grocery store aisles, apartment complex stairwells, restaurant entrances along Whittier Boulevard, or parking lots near Beverly Boulevard. A wet floor without a sign, a broken step, uneven pavement, or poor lighting can turn a routine errand into a serious injury. Los Angeles County property owners have a legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe, but proving they knew or should have known about a hazard takes evidence gathered quickly, before surveillance footage is erased or a spill is cleaned up. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we connect Montebello residents with independent personal injury attorneys who understand how to build these cases. If you were hurt on someone else's property, reaching out early can make a real difference in preserving what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Premises Liability Law

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, inspection records, and prior complaints to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Montebello stores and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partially responsible for the fall, you can still recover a share of damages. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault is argued fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Montebello?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. That window can be much shorter if a government-owned property, like a public sidewalk or city building, was involved, so it's worth checking on your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Whittier Boulevard and I'm not sure if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the fall. Your recovery would simply be adjusted to reflect your percentage of fault, so it's still worth having your case reviewed.

items.question: What should I do right after a slip and fall in Montebello?
items.answer: If possible, take photos of the hazard, note the time and location, and ask if there's surveillance video covering the area. Reporting the incident to the property manager and seeking medical attention creates a record that can support a claim later.
